subject: maths
title: Normal Nebula
description: Navigate the bell curve with z-scores and standard normal tables.

concepts.def: Bell-shaped, symmetric about mean μ, parameter σ².
X ~ N(μ, σ²) means X is normal with mean μ, variance σ².
z = (x - μ)/σ standardises a value to N(0,1).
Z ~ N(0,1); Φ(z) is its cumulative distribution.
Look up Φ(z) then use symmetry Φ(-z) = 1 - Φ(z).

options: 2σ of mean
1σ of mean
3σ of mean

mcqs.q: What does a larger standard deviation tell you about a data set?
options: The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
There are more data points in the set.
The data values are more spread out around the mean.
The mean of the data set is larger.

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
There are more data points in the set.
The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.

mcqs.q: If two variables are strongly correlated, what can you conclude?
options: There are more data points in the set.
Strong correlation means that one variable causes the other.
Strong correlation means the variables are equal in value.
They vary together — but correlation alone does not establish that one causes the other.
